title: A fallback chord when a shortcut is taken, and 'Ask Ember' in the OS launcher
owns: app/shared/shortcuts.ts, shortcut registration in app/main/main.ts (shared hunks), app/main/environment.ts keyboardRoute, the copy that names shortcuts (target-copy.ts, commands copy, home copy, setup check rows), scripts/package (the .desktop file), the macOS Dock menu and Windows jump list setup in main

items.text: Review #45(b). When another app already holds one of Ember's default shortcuts (Ask, Stop, Settings, and any other global one), Ember today points people to Settings > Comfort & access (round 1, (a)). Build: (1) a documented fallback chord per shortcut and OS (pick chords unlikely to clash, in shared/shortcuts.ts next to the defaults, with their labels and spoken words); when registering a default fails, register its fallback; if that fails too, keep today's route. (2) Everything that names a shortcut names the one Ember actually holds (default, fallback or none): the bubble's announcement and Read all route, the command window, the spoken line, the setup check rows, the greeting, home copy (round 2's bubble package made these depend on whether Ember holds the key: build on that). (3) The setup check / doctor row says when a fallback is in use ('Ctrl+Alt+Space is taken by another app, so Ask Ember is Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Space'). (4) 'Ask Ember' in the OS launcher: Windows app.setUserTasks (jump list) entry that starts Ember with an --ask argument; Linux .desktop file Actions=Ask with Exec=<ember> --ask (scripts/package's desktop entry, RPM and AppImage); macOS app.dock.setMenu with an Ask Ember item. --ask (first instance or second-instance argv) opens the ask box. Tests for registration fallback (fakes), the copy per state, the launcher entries' content, and --ask handling. forDocs: README Shortcuts lines. ciOnly: what the packaged checks should show. The ask package's note: (a) is done. Round 1 (53969aa) added Ask Ember… and Stop everything to settings. Round 2 (6606cb1): environment.ts keyboardRoute gives "access:ask" while another app holds the ask shortcut, else "access:stop". Ember started again (second-instance), the Dock (activate) and the settings shortcut all open settings through showHomeFromKeys, which sends that section request. section-request.ts maps it to p-ask / p-stop. The handle menu's Settings… is unchanged, since that is a pointer's way in. The setup check now says "open Ember again from the Start menu: its settings open at Ask Ember… and Stop everything, under Comfort & access" ("for its settings" when only the settings or microphone shortcut is taken). The greeting says "press Ctrl+Alt+E: settings opens at Ask Ember… and Stop everything". (b) is left as open work for the owner: shortcuts that can be remapped, an automatic fallback chord when one is taken, and an Ask entry in the launcher (Windows setUserTasks jump list, and .desktop Actions=Ask on Linux).
